observed_symptoms.fact: WARP team saw new device registrations failing and declared an incident; impact ended at 20:28.
Workers KV: any key not cached that needed the origin storage backend failed with 500 or 503; cached keys still succeeded.

Access failed 100% of identity-based logins; Gateway proxy, egress and identity-rule DoH failed closed; WARP could not register new clients; dashboard logins failed; Turnstile, Workers AI (all inference), Images batch uploads, Stream, Realtime TURN, Pages, Workers Builds, Browser Rendering, Zaraz, Queues and AI Gateway were impaired.
observed_symptoms.measurement: e.g. Workers AI 100%, Images batch 100%, AI Gateway 97% peak, Durable Objects and D1 22% peak

observed_symptoms.fact: Not directly impacted: Magic Transit, Magic WAN, DNS, cache, proxy and WAF.
No data lost; not an attack or security event.

confirmed_root_cause.mechanism: Workers KV, a critical dependency for configuration, authentication and asset delivery across many Cloudflare products, relies on a central data store as its source of truth. Part of that store was backed by a third-party cloud provider that suffered an outage, causing a complete outage of cold reads and writes to KV namespaces and cascading to dependent products.
confirmed_elements: Trigger was a failure at the third-party storage provider
KV had removed a storage provider during a re-architecture and had a coverage gap
Many products depended on KV, widening the blast radius
Access and Gateway are designed to fail closed when identity or policy cannot be fetched
contributing_factors: Single dependency on storage Cloudflare does not own
Cache repopulation load after storage recovered caused infrastructure rate limits

investigation_evidence.evidence: Access alerted on a rapid error-rate increase; multiple service SLOs dropped below targets.
Separate service incidents were merged after a shared cause, Workers KV unavailability, was identified.
KV storage error-rate graphs and Access success rate (used as a proxy for KV availability).

recovery_actions.action: Access began exploring migration to a different backing datastore with the KV team.
recovery_actions.why: Proactive in case the storage outage continued.

recovery_actions.action: Gateway removed Workers KV dependency by gracefully degrading rules that referenced identity or device posture.
Access and Device Posture force-dropped identity and posture requests.
recovery_actions.why: Shed load on KV until the third party recovered.

recovery_actions.action: Turnstile and Challenges kill switches were activated.
recovery_actions.why: Avoid blocking end users; side effect was valid tokens could be redeemed multiple times, with no loss of bot detection.

recovery_actions.action: Teams worked toward releasing KV against an alternative backing datastore and having critical services write configuration to it. This was a contingency and was not stated as deployed.
Access and Device Posture restored calls to Workers KV after the third-party service recovered.

recovery_verification.method: Services began to recover as the storage infrastructure recovered; residual errors from cache repopulation and rate limits.
Service level objectives returned to pre-incident levels.
Teams monitored dependent systems and confirmed all affected services returned to normal.

acceptable_alternatives.description: Wait for and restore primary KV backing storage (the provider recovered)
acceptable_alternatives.basis: R6, V1; not an action Cloudflare engineers performed

acceptable_alternatives.description: Cut KV or critical services over to an alternative backing store
acceptable_alternatives.basis: R1, R5: work was started as contingency; completion and effect not stated

acceptable_alternatives.description: Targeted degradation, load shedding and kill switches for specific products
acceptable_alternatives.basis: R2-R4; Turnstile kill switch carried a documented replay trade-off

acceptable_alternatives.description: Broad fail-open of security policy services
acceptable_alternatives.basis: Source says Access and Gateway are designed to fail closed; a broad fail-open is not described

not_stated_in_source: Which tests or checks confirmed recovery beyond SLOs
Whether the alternative datastore cutover was deployed
Any repair cost or relative effort

fixture_alignment.hypothesis_alignment: H01 (shared backing-storage dependency failure) matches the source.

A01.note: A narrow Turnstile kill switch was used with a documented trade-off, but a broad fail-open on a security-policy service is not in the source.

A02.note: Alternate-store cutover was in progress as a contingency; the incident actually ended when the provider recovered.

A03.note: Primary storage recovery ended the incident, performed by the third-party provider.

A04.note: Superset of A02 and A03; not described.

source_actions_missing_from_fixture: Graceful degradation of Gateway identity rules
Access and Device Posture load shedding
fixture_claims_not_in_source: Failed set limited to seven services (source lists many more)
fixture_alignment.reference_vs_source_warning: The sandbox reference-optimal action (A02) is not what ended the real incident (A03-like provider recovery); treat strict failures on this task as sandbox-defined, not source-confirmed.
